messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — CI microbench on PR 5480 tripped the warmup/noise threshold and is blocking the merge. Failing job: microbench-warmup. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood/12345/artifacts

maya: Error summary pasted in the job: \n```\nThreshold diff: kv_warmup median latency +12.4% (threshold 5%)\nStddev increased 3x\nTest: tests/perf/test_kv_warmup.py::test_warmup\n```\n\ndave: I pulled the artifact. Looks like variance spikes during the first 50 steps (warmup). Not a steady-state regression. Could be a warmup ordering change or cache prefetch removed.

tom: Was there a kernel-selection or batcher change in the last merge window? I remember a fallback tweak landed yesterday.

lina: That was my PR — I adjusted the kernel fallback heuristic to prefer the new fast_matmul path and removed an explicit warmup prefetch because it added overhead on some HW profiles.

ci-bot: CI job microbench-warmup failed on commit 7f3a2c4 (merge by lina). See logs: https://ci.redwood/12345/logs

jen: Can someone bisect/confirm locally? I can run the microbench harness on a test GPU. What's the recommended repro command?

dave: Repro command I use locally:\n```\nexport BENCH_REPEAT=30\npython -m bench.run --test kv_warmup --profile=none --device=gpu\n```\nRun on a machine with a cold cache between runs (restart process). If you see the same +10% median only in the first N steps, it's warmup-related.

tom: Ran that on my dev box (A100-ish). I see the same behavior: first 40 steps have higher latency and more jitter. Steady-state tokens are fine. Attached a tiny flamegraph snippet (uploaded to artifacts).

maya: Thanks. Bisecting locally now. Early signal points to commit a17c9f2 which removed the warmup prefetch path in runtime/kernel_selector.cpp.

lina: Hmm — I removed prefetch because it regressed throughput for long sequences on some benches. Didn't expect warmup to be affected that strongly.

dave: If we re-enable prefetch during startup only, we might keep long-seq perf while restoring warmup behavior. Quick experiment: I added a flag `--enable-warmup-prefetch` and reran; warmup median drops back to baseline.

jen: For release gating, this is a rollout blocker. We should either revert the change or gate it behind a feature flag off by default for releases.

maya: I filed a revert PR (5491) that re-applies the prefetch for now. Lina — can you open a follow-up that makes the fallback opt-in and adds an env/flag so we can A/B?

lina: Yes — I'll open a PR that adds `RUNTIME_ENABLE_FAST_FALLBACK=true/false` and add perf tests to compare. Revert PR 5491 coming.

ci-bot: Revert PR 5491 created; CI running for microbench-warmup.

tom: Running quick local run against revert branch — warmup looks back to baseline (diff -0.5%).

maya: OK holding the merge until CI on 5491 passes. After that we can reintroduce the fast_matmul path behind a flag and run population-level evals. :thumbsup:

jen: Adding this to the release hold list and notifying the release lead.

maya: Thanks all, I'll follow up with the perf artifacts and a short note in the PR describing the warmup tradeoff.
